raw_response:
Aiya, another year. My back isn't what it used to be, but chili is what I know, and 2.2 mu is all I have to work. Let me think through this season the way I always do.

**The land and what I'll plant**

I'm planting chili again. All 2.2 mu. My son says I should try something easier, but chili is what pays — one jin of dried chili brings more than a jin of wheat, and the buyers come right to the village. I don't know any other crop well enough at my age. No point changing now.

**Seedlings**

I'll buy seedlings from the same fellow in the next village who I've used for maybe eight, nine years now. He grows them in his greenhouse. Costs me about 200 yuan per mu but it saves me the trouble of raising seed in cold frames — my eyes aren't good enough for that careful work anymore. Good variety, the red thick-skinned kind the buyers want. I'll transplant around Grain Rain (谷雨), maybe a bit after if it's still cold — end of April, early May. My daughter-in-law helps me on weekends, and I hire two village women for two days to help transplant. Can't bend over that long by myself.

**Plastic film and beds**

I use the black plastic mulch, same as everyone. Keeps the weeds down and the soil warm early. I can't be pulling weeds all summer at my age, so the plastic is worth the 60 yuan a mu. I rent the small tractor from my nephew to make the beds — he does it in half a day for 150 yuan for my whole plot.

**Fertilizer**

Before I lay the plastic, I put down the compound fertilizer — the 15-15-15 bag, the big blue one. I use about one and a half bags per mu, that's what I've always done. A bag is 40 kg so that's 60 kg of the compound per mu. Then when the chili starts setting fruit, I scatter urea — maybe half a bag per mu, I do it twice during the summer when I water. My neighbor Old Zhao does more, he uses two bags of compound, but his land is bigger and he sells more. For me, one and a half is enough. Fertilizer has gotten expensive the last few years, I can't afford to throw money at the ground.

**Water**

I have the well share with three other households. I irrigate maybe 4 or 5 times through the summer — once right after transplanting so the seedlings take, then whenever the plants look droopy in the morning, and a couple of times when the fruit is filling. Pumping costs me electricity, maybe 40 yuan a time for my plot. If it rains good in July I skip one.

**Pests**

Chili gets aphids bad, and the anthracnose rot in wet years. I spray maybe 4, 5 times. The shop owner in town tells me what to buy — I can't read the labels, so I trust him. He's an honest fellow, been there 20 years. I spray in the early morning before it gets hot. Costs me maybe 200 yuan in chemicals for the whole plot across the season.

**Harvest**

I pick starting in late July, and keep picking every 10 days or so until the cold comes in October. My daughter-in-law comes for the big pickings. Last year I got maybe 2000 jin of fresh per mu — not my best year but not bad. I dry some on mats on the roof and sell dried for better price, sell the rest fresh to the buyer who comes with the truck.

**What I expect**

If the weather is normal — not too much rain in August, no hailstorm — I'm hoping for maybe 1000 kg of fresh per mu, or what works out to around 200 kg dried. That's what I usually get. Prices, who knows. Last year the buyer paid 8 yuan a jin dried. If it stays like that, after all my costs, I clear maybe 3000-4000 yuan per mu. Enough. My son sends money too.
